label: KQ6 answered: a 14-step macOS verification plan from preflight and install (npm install -g bladebro + bladebro doctor; standalone SHA-256 verification) through an agent-browser probe (see content/model, act click, vision --marks --json, state tabs, run @steps.json) to a real-browser probe (rb use/profile/status/on, repeat the see probe with injection disabled), each step with an expected output and a rollback (npm uninstall -g bladebro; bladebro stop; rb off; rb forget; data-root removal). Steps 7-10 are the agent-browser probe and 11-13 the real-browser probe, matching 006 REQ-001.

All browser modes expose the same five tools; real-browser mode differs only by lane selection and a disabled injection layer, so one recorded playbook covers both probes with the same see/act/vision/state commands.

On macOS the real-browser plan must avoid the default Chrome profile: rb mode profile requires closing the browser and branded Chrome 136+ refuses remote debugging on the default data directory; use clone (imported copy, source untouched, auto-refresh) or attach (caller-owned, stays open on detach).

Agent-browser isolation and cleanup are built in: the owned profile persists across orderly shutdowns, BLADE_HOME overrides the data root and BLADE_FRESH=1 requests an ephemeral profile, and bladebro stop must run after changing browser configuration because a running daemon retains its launch settings.

Real-browser signed-in probing is consent-and-profile gated: choose the profile/account before handing control, use attach to leave a caller-owned browser open, and treat profiles/sessions/artifacts as private with per-session re-capture and cookie/credential redaction — the exact constraints KQ7 turns into 004 safety-rule mitigations.

Version pin re-confirmed: releases/latest still returns v4.8.2 (published 2026-11-20T16:33:56Z, read 2026-11-21); macOS arm64 asset digest sha256:7324e502b1710f8fb0a073b1f71d3647266d986a50e7351cb4257ec4eb5d8fa8 and x64 sha256:d839f5f8a8bed8f616e68029350b1c36f8bc12ee2a16deb32b6f7df93a5a36c3, with .sha256 sidecars. Setup-table *-darwin-* names and release-asset *-macos-* aliases share identical digests.

bladebro doctor resolves the macOS data root (~/.local/state/blade or legacy ~/.blade) and is the verification step that confirms the browser and path before the probes; that same path is what full rollback removes.

MCP-lane verification step registers mcpServers.bladebro with args [mcp] (or npx -y bladebro mcp) and checks that the five mcp__bladebro__ tools appear after client restart; rollback is removing the entry and restarting — the KQ2 fallback now cast as a verification step.
Verification is authoring the step list only: installing Bladebro or running live probes is an operator stop-for-yes owned by phase 006 and an explicit research non-goal.
Every upstream Bladebro claim stays pinned to v4.8.2 (published 2026-11-20T16:33:56Z) and the 2026-11-21 read date; flags are re-verified against the installed binary because upstream moves fast.
